Random Forest Epigenetic Predictor¶

CV and SHAP analysis¶

optimised parameters (max_leaf_nodes= 50 & min_samples_leaf= 100,) random seed = 8 for shuffling

Step1: Train the model¶

In [9]:
# set up model to run
estimator = RandomForestRegressor(
    n_estimators = 10000, #default 100 but we need more
    criterion= "squared_error", #default
    max_leaf_nodes= 50, #equivalent to max_leaves in lgbm
    min_samples_leaf= 100, #equivalent to min_data in lgbm
)
#shuffle rows
epi, y = shuffle(epi, y, random_state=8)
In [10]:
#output metrics to collect
score_list = ['neg_root_mean_squared_error',#average error in logFC units RMSE
                                    'r2',#coefficent of determination; correlation score
                                    'max_error' #worst case error
                                   ]
In [11]:
scores = cross_validate(estimator, epi, y, cv=10,
                       scoring = score_list,
                        return_estimator = True,
                        return_indices = True)
In [12]:
gif, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.boxplot(scores["test_r2"])
ax.set_xticklabels(['r2'])

gif, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.boxplot(scores["test_neg_root_mean_squared_error"])
ax.set_xticklabels(['-RMSE'])

gif, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.boxplot(scores["test_max_error"])
ax.set_xticklabels(['max_error'])

In [14]:
sdict = {}
model_name = "A6H_7"
sdict[model_name +"_fit_time"] = scores["fit_time"]
for s in score_list:
    if s == "neg_root_mean_squared_error":
        short_name = "rmse"
    else:
        short_name = s
    sdict[model_name + "_" + short_name] = scores["test_"+s]
    

sdf = pd.DataFrame(sdict)
print(sdf.head())
sns.scatterplot(sdf, x='A6H_7_r2', y='A6H_7_rmse').set_title("7 feature model optimised");
